VALIDATION.md.text:
# Release validation and provenance

## Current candidate scope and pending qualification

The initial router/Pages-only v1.17.2 candidate was prepared from main `d01c40121752f09660f8083c6c2a967acbf714ab` and merged in PR #1580 as `e1c36c8f555aa92a9587e30b3c93aa04ea786c00` (tree `01bbac0e382aa0e02fa7a63efd4543c9e95aaadd`). Its original [preparation text and byte identity](history/initial-preparation.json) are preserved. That source and its seven successful workflows are historical, not qualification of this expanded candidate.

The expanded v1.17.2 source includes the Alpha project transfer merged in [PR #1578](https://github.com/MontrealAI/AGIJobManager/pull/1578), website source-edition/sitemap guidance, and the recoverable bilingual Builder introduced by [PR #1582](https://github.com/MontrealAI/AGIJobManager/pull/1582). The PR's initial head `41723365006860fcd03397961843f01e29429819` (tree `861d95c747fd3166a1c794158291dabfa4fd014d`) identifies that input only; subsequent fixes, release gates and metadata require a newly reviewed final source. The later input `a75e439b12d89b365b1678fd3fe1d214b244c041` (tree `3956e9da98f48e1c2a21ccd32cbd507df7a8957c`) adds strict UTF-8/BOM rejection and immutable Builder-source selection. The subsequent input `493e7467f787fadc883a873322e6ed1f3c7e9a21` (tree `9eb8d09453c06420351f4afce56603746bc0edbc`) adds clear-history protection and selects real Builder code `8c3b3f23260113dd421790336f561bc24e2ad44d` (tree `b2238683b73b732036d5fcdc4aa63d3481b84b2f`). The release-wrapper correction published as `7e73fdb9e92b16bea35ef25ce99d92076a6e9d36` (tree `2406d7570b31ad606899051b2e6db25712bfcf46`) preserved that complete selected source and selector unchanged; the later source update below supersedes that selection. The intermediate local correction at `2c2e7fd4e94e7e5ae78971765aa2c5dc1b76d56a` (tree `9072dc002ebc4dff82777f51c020297e53348e55`) and its 75 release-gate cases are superseded historical preparation, never published qualification. No initial PR, intermediate local candidate or earlier-main receipt qualifies later edits.

All eight qualification workflows must pass on the exact final main source: CI, UI CI, Docs Integrity, Security Verification, Mainnet USDC Fork Qualification, Release Candidate Preparation, GitHub Pages, and Alpha project handoff. The publisher checks each workflow identity, main push event, commit, completed successful required jobs/steps and unique checkout log marker. The handoff and Pages qualification workflows run on every main push and main-targeting PR, including metadata-only edits, and the handoff must execute the pinned native validator checkout, receiver/browser-adapter and source-identity tests. Missing, wrong-head, failed, skipped or incomplete handoff evidence blocks publication automatically.

The separate internal optional-router review (585 preflight cases and 23 additional probes) concerns its recorded source only. The reported 4,212-byte router runtime is source-compiled evidence, not deployed-address verification.

The root, Hardhat and UI version labels change only from 1.17.1 to 1.17.2. Dependency resolutions, all Solidity and compiler settings remain unchanged. `config/next-deployment-contract-changes.json` retains the historical baseline and declares exact current package hashes. The executed v1.17.1 cutover report is preserved byte for byte in `docs/qualification/history/mainnet-cutover-v1.17.1.json`. The current `mainnet-cutover-next-deployment.json` updates only its four package hashes and remains an expected comparison fixture until a fresh fork execution matches it. Historical outcomes and block identity are unchanged; no fresh fork execution is implied by this source-binding update.

The v1.17.1 Slither review remains untouched. The separate v1.17.2 review updates only the root-lockfile hash and retains every finding disposition. Its pending status is explicit. Final-source Security Verification must actually rerun all three scanners and compare exact source hashes and finding identities; copied historical findings are not new scan results or an independent audit.

## Historical initial-scope local preparation — 15 October 2026

Using Node 22.23.2, the initial scope at local commit `7cb1b10d635a81ff8d5ab60e2a624cac6cc51035` and tree `01bbac0e382aa0e02fa7a63efd4543c9e95aaadd` passed 585 preflight cases, 60 offline release-gate cases (normal and optimized Python), dependency/source-boundary checks, 11 Slither-verifier adversarial cases, documentation/ENS/UI-documentation checks, 38 Builder cases, three preservation cases and 35 mocked console checks. The UI artifact was built twice from clean Next.js state and compared byte for byte. Pages build/inventory checks and English/French browser journeys passed with the available Chromium 139.0.7258.5 executable; the initially requested Playwright-managed executable was absent, so that fallback is recorded explicitly. The hosted pinned-browser lane remains required. These are focused local preparation results, not final-main qualification or live-chain evidence.

An exact-byte comparison preserved 302 existing release/history/static-review records, all Solidity/compiler/deployment source, and all six package dependency graphs. Only software version labels changed in those package files. The fork expected fixture changes four package hashes; its other 72 hashes and all historical outcomes remain identical. The new static-review binding changes only the root-lockfile hash; all 163 retained finding dispositions remain identical across the three report inventories.

The top-level archive guide copies rebase their relative links to included source documents while source copies remain unchanged. Six focused cases cover parent paths, sibling guides, external links, fragments/queries, missing/escaping targets and the complete current four-guide set.

## Expanded Builder scope and pending final evidence

The native Alpha transfer and bilingual UI retain the original public-data dossier and complete history, require explicit mapping/rights confirmation, run local work and prepare a separately priced unfunded USDC draft. Browser save/recovery and source exports do not authorize provider use, production admission, independent review, payment or activation. The initial PR reports focused native/browser/worker checks and separate engineering/EN-FR QA; those are source-specific preparation claims, not final-main qualification, and are not added to the historical counts above.

Final qualification must exercise the new handoff lane and Pages browser recovery/export journeys on the reviewed source. The pinned Alpha validator's Apache-2.0 and nested MIT provenance are included. Editable source remains offline-rebuildable, and compressed source inventory is checked against its declared byte length and digest. No contract source, compiler setting, package version or lockfile is changed by the Builder/gate addition.

The Pages inventory is generated, not a fixed whitelist of 26 files. This scope adds `successor/downloads/MANAGER_CONTEXT.json`, producing 27 public entries in `build-info.json.files`; verify the actual final inventory and every entry's digest. `build-info.json` itself is checked separately, and `.nojekyll` remains in `buildOnlyFiles`. The same generated context is included inside the COMPLETE ZIP and compared byte for byte after clean-source reconstruction; it does not add a tenth standalone release asset. Generated Builder outputs remain a closed five-file inventory, of which four are standalone release assets.

## Later immutable source and local package reconciliation — 16 October 2026

The later PR input `80bb7a90cf10d3fb40793bdf1170deb63c1453a9` (tree `52032079b7876b0ba70733f5e36aba2c746db0da`) descends from the published release wrapper and retains its eight-workflow publisher gates, strict archive-context bridge and closed output inventory. It selects real Builder code `ab516fbd32fd7cf1a9620fd630947fee1455fca2` (tree `b011643b56115c5baa39ca796cbf0a944c152eda`, engine SHA-256 `0cc9fe36376b10232c53e2b2dd87e0264f368bace07b499f185f83fa3361f4d0`). The selector-only commit does not change that complete selected source closure. The previous `8c3b3f23` selection and its preparation counts remain historical.

This source preserves pending inspected project bytes through language changes and cancelled or invalid replacement files, requires fresh confirmation, and protects a pending saved copy from clear/overwrite. Cross-tab storage loss or replacement preserves the exact in-memory copies and rearms leave protection. An inspected copy can be downloaded separately from the active workspace. Browser runs reserve checkpoint eight for the separately priced USDC draft; existing full eight-checkpoint histories remain readable, savable and exportable with explicit terminal guidance. Download requests alone still do not prove a durable save.

Exact-byte reconstruction verified all 1,368 tracked source objects and modes against the complete remote tree and verified the actual selected Git commit/tree. With Node 22.23.2, this exact input passed 585 preflight cases, 87 release-gate cases in normal and optimized Python, dependency/source-boundary checks, documentation/ENS checks, and 22 site/preservation cases. Fourteen additional checks extracted the exact UI handlers and exercised mocked storage/download/cancellation behavior; they are not native-browser results.

Two independent assemblies of this exact input produced byte-identical eight-file candidate sets. The COMPLETE ZIP is 30,773,732 bytes with 1,379 inventoried payloads, including 1,368 archived source objects. Clean extraction passed the complete inventory, five-output offline rebuild, 17 portable cases, 35 mocked console cases and 87 release gates. Both English/French embedded source inventories match the 37-file editable ZIP and independently reconstruct the selected source context, whose `MANAGER_CONTEXT.json` SHA-256 is `695a94ca2b1e3e100c4258a8ed360c27253bf561e3995f8f368d0c6f24010215`. The source manifest contains 34 selected code/license inputs; package metadata, strict `SOURCE.json` and rebuild instructions make up the other three editable entries. Normal Pages assembly reports 27 public files and a separate build-only `.nojekyll`. English/French Builder pages are 744,900/746,888 bytes, below the unchanged 750,000-byte gate. These counts and hashes describe the `80bb7a90` input, not later documentation commits or final-main assets.

The primary native-inclusive local Node run passed 63 of 65 cases. Two environment-sensitive cases were then checked separately without changing source: the CLI error-JSON case passes with warnings suppressed for that diagnostic invocation, because the original stderr included the environment's experimental proxy warning; the hidden-edit fixture passes in an isolated ordinary Git repository, whereas the retained sparse Alpha worktree exposed an edit that the fixture expected index flags to hide. The original failures remain part of the evidence; these reruns are not represented as one clean full-suite pass. Actual EN/FR native transfers, Node/browser-adapter parity, source-drift rejection and replacement-tree rejection pass against pinned Alpha commit `7c410d3d61d5d6bba5354307e1784dba2b3aa177`. No new local browser was launched. Hosted native/browser and all eight exact-final-main workflows remain required; local package success and earlier PR checks do not qualify a later source, publication or live deployment.

## Separate Builder and release identities

`RELEASE_MANIFEST.json.sourceCommit/sourceTree`, `QUALIFICATION.json`, workflow markers, candidate artifact names, attestations and `build-info.json.sourceCommit` identify the exact final wrapper/main checkout. The Builder's `SOURCE_MANIFEST.json`, `MANAGER_CONTEXT.json`, embedded HTML source and editable archive identify the separately selected immutable Builder code commit. These identities need not be equal. The tracked `config/successor-builder-source.json` binds the selected commit, tree, version and complete ordered inventory digest; normal assembly verifies those real Git objects and all selected source bytes without bootstrap, replacement refs or inherited Git redirection.

`RELEASE_MANIFEST.json.builderSource` retains the exact strict v2 editable-source context derived by that verifier. Assembly and offline verification cross-check it against the archived selector, selected package checksum/version, complete source inventory and standalone/context manifests. Only temporary Git-free reconstruction receives a synthesized `SOURCE.json`; archived Git source remains unchanged. Both English/French HTML source exports and the editable ZIP retain the same complete context. Offline reconstruction checks supplied byte identity, not independent publication or authorship. Missing, malformed, substituted, relabelled, reordered or unexpected context must fail closed.

A change to Builder code requires a real code commit followed by a selector commit using that code commit's actual SHA/tree and inventory digest. The branch must not move to the inconsistent intermediate commit. Documentation/release-wrapper changes may retain the selected Builder identity only when the verified source closure and selected package bytes remain unchanged. Final-main qualification always applies to the wrapper after the selector is resolved.

## Release gates

Candidate assets must be built twice and compared, then extracted and rebuilt without network dependencies. Contract regressions, native historical-runtime reconstruction, pinned USDC/ENS fork tests, Foundry fuzz/invariants, source-bound static-analysis review, UI, documentation and pinned Alpha project handoff gates all remain required. Local focused checks do not replace these workflows. `QUALIFICATION.json` must bind completed exact-final-source runs and the immutable candidate artifact; no qualification receipt is created by this preparation.

Download all nine published assets into one directory. Use a trusted checkout of the reviewed release source to verify every asset's assembly attestation, then checksums and the published inventory:

```bash
gh attestation verify My-SUCCESSOR-Omega-en.html --repo MontrealAI/AGIJobManager --signer-workflow MontrealAI/AGIJobManager/.github/workflows/publish-v114.yml --signer-digest EXACT_RELEASE_COMMIT --source-digest EXACT_RELEASE_COMMIT --source-ref refs/heads/main --deny-self-hosted-runners
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt
python3 scripts/release/verify-package.py PATH_TO_DOWNLOADED_ASSETS --published
```

Repeat attestation verification for every asset. Attestation lookup needs network access; the package verifier is offline. Without `--published`, it accepts only the eight-file candidate inventory. Published mode requires `QUALIFICATION.json`; never remove it or edit checksums to make a download pass. Publication must report `immutable: true` and repository/workflow/source-bound attestations.

After separately authorized Pages publication, compare `build-info.json` and every `files` entry against the same reviewed SHA. `.nojekyll` is a local build marker under `buildOnlyFiles`; the uploader excludes it from public deployment. Preserve the immutable v1.17.1 release and all A1–A5 activation records. Actual-address router verification, owner configuration, current-chain readiness and live operation remain separate and unestablished here.

START_HERE.md.text:
# Start here — AGIJobManager v1.17.2

To continue a native public-data Alpha project, use the [Builder](../../successor/README.md) and [Alpha transfer guide](../../successor/ALPHA_PROJECT_HANDOFF.md). Inspect the original dossier, confirm row/unit mapping and rights, run local work, then enter a separate USDC price for an unfunded draft. Save locally or verify exported files before closing; recovery requires fresh confirmation and grants no payment or production authority.

Use the [optional metadata-router guide](../../DEPLOYMENT/OPTIONAL_METADATA_ROUTER.md) only if that helper is needed. Review the original journal and exact-source verification requirements before any separately authorized deployment or recovery request. A verified router is still unconfigured. Source qualification does not establish a live address's explorer status or operational readiness.

For the manager itself, follow the [second-deployment checklist](../../DEPLOYMENT/SECOND_MAINNET_RELEASE.md), [scoped qualification decision](../../DEPLOYMENT/SECOND_MAINNET_QUALIFICATION_DECISION.md) and [Hardhat guide](../../../hardhat/README.md). Preserve the original instance, its jobs/claims and its original compiler/deployment records.

The COMPLETE ZIP includes source, contracts, deployment scripts, tests and operator guides. Standalone USDC and English/French SUCCESSOR Builder assets remain included. Local Builder work needs no wallet, account or provider key. The previous immutable v1.17.1 assets remain available unchanged.

See [validation](VALIDATION.md), [release notes](RELEASE_NOTES.md), [recovery](RECOVERY_GUIDE.md) and the [Pages inventory guide](../../ui/GITHUB_PAGES.md). This software candidate does not authorize public-chain transactions, owner configuration or paid intake.

RECOVERY_GUIDE.md.text:
# Recovery and rollback

Never overwrite the only copy of the first deployment's source, artifacts, compiler input or journal. Keep existing jobs, review credits, bonds and deferred claims on their original manager. A new deployment does not migrate them.

A failed deployment command may already have broadcast. Reconcile its unique journal and canonical receipts before any retry; rerunning deployment does not resume the old attempt. Follow the Hardhat guide's keyless verification recovery and the operator incident-response guide. Do not edit receipt success fields or bypass readiness failures.

Fresh deployment starts paused. Preserve ownership acceptance and readiness evidence separately. Pausing intake does not pause ordinary settlement; settlement pause delays exits and lifecycle clocks. Use the intended owner's incident policy and reconcile reserved liabilities before any separately authorized action.

For local Builder work, retain downloaded HTML, the original Alpha dossier and complete-history capsules before changes. Requesting a download does not confirm that it was saved. Use explicit browser save when available, keep a verified exported copy, and confirm the mapping again after loading a saved transfer. Clearing a saved browser copy marks retained open history as unsaved; an empty workspace stays clean. Clearing browser storage is not a backup; quota or unavailable storage must not be treated as a successful save. Rollback restores a chosen local version; it cannot reverse payments or completed external effects. Keep durable worker history and reconcile uncertain outcomes before another authorized attempt.

For a software regression, use a reviewed correction, repeat qualification and publish a new version. Never move a published tag or replace release assets. Website publication, deployed-contract changes and intake activation each require their own authorization.

For the optional metadata router, preserve its original non-overwriting journal. Use only the guide's existing-address recovery path after reconciling canonical creation/runtime evidence. A `verified_unconfigured` result does not authorize attaching it to a manager or changing metadata settings. Never treat a failed explorer request as permission to deploy a replacement.

Recover Builder sources using the complete exported inventory and its strict v2 `SOURCE.json`, including selected commit/tree, package checksum and full source manifest. Do not replace its selected commit with a later website/release wrapper SHA. The release manifest records both identities; the archived selector and all source bytes must agree before an offline rebuild. A source edit requires a newly reviewed real code commit and subsequent selector update.

RELEASE_NOTES.md.text:
# Recoverable Alpha project Builder and guarded router verification

This unpublished edition combines native Alpha project transfers and the recoverable English/French local Builder with the optional `AGIJobPages` metadata-router tooling merged in [PR #1579](https://github.com/MontrealAI/AGIJobManager/pull/1579), and corrects the public Pages file inventory. It changes no Solidity source, compiler setting, dependency resolution, ABI, settlement rule or deployed contract. The immutable v1.17.1 tag, assets and historical qualification records remain unchanged.

## Native Alpha project transfer and recovery

The [Alpha project handoff](../../successor/ALPHA_PROJECT_HANDOFF.md) validates the pinned native public-data dossier, retains its original bytes, project/cycle identity and complete history, and requires explicit row/unit mapping and rights confirmation. Node and closed browser-worker adapters perform the same replay. Users run actual local work, then enter a separate six-decimal USDC price to export an unfunded draft; importing a project grants no authority, independent approval, payment or production admission.

The bilingual Builder adds explicit browser save/load/clear controls, fresh confirmation after reload, original-dossier and complete-history exports, and editable offline sources. A requested download does not prove that a durable file was saved; retain the original dossier and verify exports before closing. Browser storage may be unavailable, cleared or quota-limited. The pinned Alpha validator is retained unchanged with Apache-2.0 provenance and the nested Jobs compiler's MIT license. Compressed trusted editable-source inventory is byte-length/hash checked; unsupported decompression leaves project JSON exports available. These vendored sources do not change npm dependency resolutions.

## Router tooling, packaging and Pages

The [optional-router guide](../../DEPLOYMENT/OPTIONAL_METADATA_ROUTER.md) covers explicit read-only planning, guarded deployment, canonical constructor/runtime checks, explorer verification and non-overwriting recovery journals. Successful verification produces a `verified_unconfigured` receipt. The helper remains optional and is not attached to a manager; owner configuration and intake activation need their own authorization. Actual-address explorer verification remains pending until an authorized deployment produces evidence. Tests and a source-compiled 4,212-byte runtime are not a live verification receipt or an independent audit.

The Pages builder retains the empty local `.nojekyll` marker under `buildOnlyFiles`, while `files` lists only public artifacts. The GitHub Pages uploader excludes dotfiles, so the inventory no longer promises a public `.nojekyll` URL. Native same-document fragment navigation is also covered by the merged browser wait correction; normal document navigation keeps its existing wait behavior.

Builder source identity is selected by a tracked immutable commit/tree/inventory pin and remains stable across documentation-only wrappers. The release and Pages source identity still identifies the actual final checkout. Packaging records the verified selected v2 context under `RELEASE_MANIFEST.json.builderSource`, checks it against archived source/selector/package bytes, and reproduces the five generated outputs offline. Strict BOM and malformed UTF-8 imports are rejected without normalization. Clearing a saved browser copy keeps retained in-memory history protected as unsaved work.

Top-level archive guides retain usable links to the included source documentation; the source copies stay unchanged. The nine published assets remain unchanged as an inventory contract. Generated `MANAGER_CONTEXT.json` is retained inside the COMPLETE ZIP and verified against a clean source rebuild, without adding a tenth standalone asset. Pages inventories are generated from actual output: the new `successor/downloads/MANAGER_CONTEXT.json` increases this candidate from 26 to 27 public file entries. Verify every generated `files` entry against the final source rather than accepting an old fixed count; `.nojekyll` remains build-only.

Root, deployment and UI software labels and generated guides are aligned to v1.17.2. A version-only source-binding update preserves earlier fork outcomes and reviewed static findings as expected comparison fixtures, not newly executed evidence. All eight exact-final-main workflows, reproducible packaging and final publication provenance remain mandatory. The automated publisher now requires the Alpha project handoff run, exact checkout marker and successful receiver steps in addition to the original seven lanes; missing, stale or failed handoff evidence blocks publication. See [validation](VALIDATION.md).

No contract deployment, manager configuration, provider spending, ownership change or activation is included. Existing instances, obligations and original journals remain on their recorded source. The owner's scoped external-review/Sepolia omissions for the second deployment remain recorded in the [qualification decision](../../DEPLOYMENT/SECOND_MAINNET_QUALIFICATION_DECISION.md); automated checks do not become an external independent security review.
